# Harbour

> A minimal web app that displays your task tracker's projects and issues as a collapsible tree with a CLI aesthetic. Backed by Linear, GitHub, GitHub Projects, Jira, or a local store.

## Overview

- Syncs with your workspace's provider (Linear, GitHub, GitHub Projects, Jira, or a local store) via OAuth or token auth
- Supports multiple workspaces
- Displays projects and issues in a tree structure with box-drawing characters

## Navigation

- **Workspace selector**: `workspace: {name}` in nav bar - click to switch
- **View switcher**: `.nav-views` row in the header - switch between views (observation/swipe/swim/settings + flag-gated roadmap/dispatch/proxy); at the top of the page, reachable without scrolling on mobile
- **Team filter**: `team: {name}` in nav bar - filter issues by team
- **Expand/collapse**: Click task row or ▶/▼ arrow
- **Project collapse**: Click project header
- **Reset**: Click "reset" to restore default view state

## Status Indicators

- ○ (todo) - `data-status="todo"` - Ready to start (planned for soon)
- ◌ (backlog) - `data-status="backlog"` - In the queue (not coming soon)
- ◐ (in-progress) - `data-status="in-progress"` - In progress
- ✓ (done) - `data-status="done"` - Completed

## DOM Structure

### Landmarks
- `main` - main content area
- `[role="region"][aria-label="In Progress Tasks"]` - in-progress section
- `[role="region"][aria-label="Projects"]` - projects section

### Node Container Structure
Issues are wrapped in nested `.node` containers:
```
.node[data-id="{id}"]           - node container
  .line[data-id="{id}"]         - task row (keyboard-operable: role=button, tabindex=0, aria-expanded)
  .details[data-details-for]    - details panel (hidden by default)
    .detail-toggle[data-toggle="details"] - "Details ▶" toggle
    .detail-content[data-content="details"] - description + metadata (hidden)
      .detail-toggle[data-toggle="comments"] - "Comments ▶" toggle (auth only, nested)
      .detail-toggle[data-toggle="attachments"] - "Attachments (N) ▶" toggle (auth only, nested; image gallery via /api/image relay, attachment-capable providers only)
      .detail-toggle[data-toggle="brief"]    - "Brief ▶" toggle (auth only, nested; lazy AI brief)
      .detail-toggle[data-toggle="recap"]    - "Recap ▶" toggle (auth only, nested; lazy AI recap)
      .detail-toggle[data-toggle="scan"]     - "Scan ▶" toggle (auth only, nested; human-triggered scan for an operator-worthy blocker, no auto-run)
      .detail-toggle[data-toggle="context"] - "Context ▶" toggle (auth only, nested; lazy relationship diagram)
      .detail-toggle[data-toggle="sessions"] - "Dispatched Sessions ▶" toggle (nested; dispatch flag only)
    .detail-toggle[data-toggle="prompts"]  - "Prompts ▶" toggle (auth only)
    .detail-content[data-content="prompts"] - prompt buttons (hidden)
    .detail-link                - "View in {provider} →" link (provider name is dynamic, e.g. "View in Linear")
  .children                     - container for nested child nodes
    .node[data-id="{child-id}"] - child node (same structure)
```

### Detail Section Toggles
When a task is expanded, its details contain toggleable sections:
- **Details ▶**: Description and metadata (assignee, dates, labels)
- **Prompts ▶**: Prompt buttons and AI features (authenticated users only)
- **View in {provider} →**: Navigation link (always visible; provider name is dynamic, e.g. "View in Linear"). Same provider-aware text on the swim/ship popovers.

Toggle behavior:
- Both sections start collapsed (▶ arrow)
- Click toggle to expand (▼ arrow) and show content
- Toggle state is per-issue and does not persist across page loads
- Same task in different sections (In Progress vs Project) has independent toggles

### Task Selectors
Both In Progress and Projects sections use the same nested structure:
- `.node[data-id="{id}"]` - node container wrapping line, details, and children
- `.node > .line` - task row element within a node
- `.node > .details` - details panel (sibling of .line within same node)
- `.node > .children` - container for nested child nodes
- `[data-id="{issue-id}"]` - task by issue ID (on both .node and .line; the provider's own canonical id, not Linear-specific)
- `[data-testid="issue-line"]` - stable task-row hook (on .line; pair with `[data-id]` for a specific issue)
- `[data-testid="issue-source"]` - per-task source flag, e.g. `data-source="github"` (present only in a multi-provider workspace; absent for single-source/Linear-only)
- `[data-testid="project"][data-project-name="{name}"]` - project card by name (`[data-testid="project-header"]` on its header)
- `[data-identifier="{LIN-123}"]` - task by Linear identifier (on .line element)
- `[data-status="todo|in-progress|done"]` - filter by status
- `[data-section="in-progress|project"]` - scope to section (expand state is independent per section)
- `[data-parent="{id}"]` - parent ID (on .line element)
- `[data-depth="{n}"]` - nesting level (0 = top-level, on .line element)
- `.expandable` - tasks that can be expanded; keyboard-operable controls (role=button, tabindex=0, Enter/Space to toggle, aria-expanded reflects state)
- `.in-progress-project` - project name badge shown in brackets for In Progress items

### Traversing the Tree
- Find node by ID: `.node[data-id="{id}"]`
- Find node's details: `.node[data-id="{id}"] > .details`
- Find node's direct children: `.node[data-id="{id}"] > .children > .node`
- Find all descendants: `.node[data-id="{id}"] .node`

### Project Selectors
- `.project[data-id="{project-id}"]` - project container
- `.project-header` - clickable project header
- `[data-completed-for="{project-id}"]` - completed tasks section
- `[data-testid="create-task"]` - create-task affordance (project level, authenticated only). For providers with in-app create support (ui.inlineCreate) this is a plain link, `[data-testid="create-task-trigger"]`, navigating to the dedicated task-create page `/workspace/{urlKey}/task/new?projectId={projectId}`. Providers with only an external deep-link instead render `[data-action="create-task"]` (a `target="_blank"` link) with no `/task/new` involved. On the create page, `[data-testid="task-create-form"]` holds EXACTLY the provider's declared `createFields()` — never a fixed set — so which of these appear varies by provider: `[data-testid="task-create-title"]` (always), `[data-testid="task-create-description"]`, `[data-testid="task-create-teamId"]`, `[data-testid="task-create-projectId"]`, `[data-testid="task-create-stateId"]`, `[data-testid="task-create-priority"]`. Each of teamId/projectId/stateId is a `<select>` of the provider's real ids when the list is available, or a text input fallback when it isn't (never a 500). Picking a team (Linear only — states are team-scoped) resubmits the page as a GET with `?teamId=` to rescope the state list. Submitting POSTs `/workspace/{urlKey}/api/issues` and returns to the dashboard; a submitted stateId/priority the provider didn't declare a control for is rejected 400. `labels` never appears on this page.
- `[data-testid="issue-edit-link"]` - edit affordance inside an issue's Details (only when the provider supports in-app edit, ui.inlineEdit). A plain link, not a toggle: it navigates to the dedicated task-edit page `/workspace/{urlKey}/task/{issueId}/edit`, which accepts either a UUID or an identifier like `LIN-123`. On that page, `[data-testid="task-edit-form"]` holds the four editable fields — `[data-testid="task-edit-title"]`, `[data-testid="task-edit-description"]`, `[data-testid="task-edit-stateId"]` (a `<select>` of the provider's workflow states, or a text input when the provider cannot supply them), `[data-testid="task-edit-priority"]` — plus `[data-testid="task-edit-submit"]` and `[data-testid="task-edit-cancel"]`. The description field has a Write/Preview toggle (LIN-1575): `[data-testid="task-edit-tab-write"]` / `[data-testid="task-edit-tab-preview"]` swap `[data-testid="task-edit-description"]` (the raw Markdown textarea, still the sole source submitted) against `[data-testid="task-edit-preview"]` (a read-only rendered pane); switching tabs never mutates the textarea's value, so saving while Preview is showing still submits the raw Markdown. The pair is a real ARIA tablist, so `role=tab` selection ("Write" / "Preview") works too, and `aria-selected` tells you which is active. Saving PATCHes `/workspace/{urlKey}/api/issues/{issueId}` and returns to the dashboard. An unknown id renders `[data-testid="task-edit-not-found"]` with a 404.
- `.project[data-project-type="periodicals"]` - synthetic Periodicals group (recurring maintenance templates, not Linear issues; workspace-flag gated). Its rows expand to a dispatchable prompt; they have no Linear URL and no "Add task" link.

### Search Selectors
- `.search-toggle` - opens/closes search panel (in nav bar's `.nav-actions`)
- `#search-panel` - search input panel (below the page title, not the nav bar; LIN-1512)
- `#search-input` - text input for keyword search
- `.search-clear` / `#search-clear` - clears search and restores full view
- `#search-no-results` - "no matching issues" message (shown when search has zero results)
- `[data-search-text]` - lowercased searchable content on each `.line` (title, description, assignee, ID, labels)

### Navigation Selectors
- `#workspace-toggle` - workspace dropdown button
- `#team-toggle` - team dropdown button
- `#workspace-options` - workspace dropdown panel
- `#team-options` - team dropdown panel
- `[data-team="{id}"]` - team filter option (use "all" for all teams)
- `.nav-views` - header-level cross-view switcher row (LIN-978); single scrolling row at the top of every workspace page
- `[data-testid="nav-view-{name}"]` - a view-switcher link by its visible text (e.g. `observation`, `swipe`, `swim`, `settings`, and the flag-gated `roadmap`/`dispatch`/`proxy`); the active view renders as a `<strong class="nav-view-current">` instead of an `<a>`. First-class views always show; power-user views only with their per-user flag; experimental views appear in the `⋯ more` overflow group when their own flag is on (same gated-inclusion policy as power-user views, not Settings-only)

### Footer Selectors
- `.page-footer` - footer container
- `.footer-actions` - container for the `reset` action (authenticated pages only; the cross-view links moved to the header `.nav-views` switcher in LIN-978)
- `.footer-action` - action link (reset)
- `.reset-view` - reset button (in footer)
- `.footer-deploy` - deploy information container
- `.footer-link` - link within deploy info (commit hash or GitHub repo)
- `.footer-ai-status` - AI connection status indicator
- `.footer-ai-status.free` - free tier status (yellow, shows "ai: ● free (N/20)")
- `[data-ai-source]` - AI source attribute on footer status (`oauth`, `env`, `free`)
- `.footer-ai-model` / `[data-ai-model]` - workspace LLM model name, filled client-side from `/api/recommend/status`
- `[data-testid="footer-feedback-toggle"]` - simple "feedback" link in the footer legal row (alongside privacy/terms) that toggles the feedback widget (`data-enabled="true|false"`); persists the per-user `feedbackWidget` flag via `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/settings/features`
- `[data-testid="feedback-widget-root"]` - feedback widget mount (`data-enabled` reflects the flag); the popup is built client-side only when enabled
- `[data-testid="nav-feedback-trigger"]` - feedback trigger in the nav bar's `.nav-actions` row (opens the popup; `aria-expanded` tracks it). LIN-2298 moved this out of the fixed `.feedback-fab` it replaces: the FAB was a `position: fixed` element over full-width content, which LIN-2272 proved no CSS reserve can clear at every scroll offset. There is no floating feedback button any more.
- `[data-testid="feedback-popup"]` - feedback popup; `feedback-message` (textarea), `feedback-priority` (0-4 select), `feedback-file` (screenshot), `feedback-minimize` (keeps draft), `feedback-submit` → `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/feedback`

### Interactive Elements
- `.toggle` - expand/collapse arrow for child tasks (▶/▼)
- `.detail-toggle` - expand/collapse toggle for detail sections (Details ▶ / Prompts ▶)
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="details"]` - Details section toggle
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="prompts"]` - Prompts section toggle
- `.detail-content[data-content="details"]` - Details section content (hidden by default)
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="comments"]` - Comments toggle (nested in Details, lazy-loaded on first expand)
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="brief"]` - Brief toggle (nested in Details, lazy AI current-state brief)
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="recap"]` - Recap toggle (nested in Details, lazy AI progress recap)
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="scan"]` - Scan toggle (nested in Details, human-triggered scan for an operator-worthy blocker; never auto-runs on expand — only a cheap status check does. A found blocker renders a question + options + an answer box (durable comment write) and a dismiss action.)
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="context"]` - Context toggle (nested in Details, lazy relationship diagram: blockers/blocked/parent/children/related). Each task node is `.context-node` with `data-context-nav="LIN-123"`.
- `.detail-toggle[data-toggle="sessions"]` - Dispatched Sessions toggle (nested in Details, dispatch flag only)
- `.detail-content[data-content="prompts"]` - Prompts section content (hidden by default)
- `.in-progress-header` - collapsible section header

## Workflow Labels

Tasks use 1 workflow label:

**`bug`** - Investigating unexpected behavior
- Use when investigating unexpected behavior
- Document reproduction steps and hypotheses
- Remove when bug is fixed

Blocked-ness is NOT a label. A task is blocked when it has an incomplete
`blocks`/`blocked-by` relationship to another task — record blockers as a
relationship between the tasks, not as a label.

### Label Rules

1. **Remove when done**: Remove the `bug` label when its purpose is complete
2. **Blocking is a relationship**: capture blockers via `blocks`/`blocked-by`
   relations, never a label

### Typical Flow

1. New task arrives → it is Ready once it's in a backlog/unstarted state
2. Work begins → set status to "In Progress"
3. If blocked → add a `blocks`/`blocked-by` relationship to the blocking task
4. If bug found → add `bug` label
5. Work complete → set status to "Done"

### Readiness Checks

- `blocked`: "Can work resume based on this analysis?"
- `bug`: "Could someone implement a fix based on this?"

**DOM Selectors:**
- `.label-prompt[data-issue-id][data-label]` - clickable label that generates a prompt
- `.prompt-container[data-prompt-for="{id}"]` - container for generated prompt
- `.prompt-text` - the prompt text (inside container)
- `.prompt-copy` - copy button (inside container)
- `.prompt-download` - download button (inside container); saves the prompt as a `.md` file. Use this instead of copy for very large prompts (e.g. retro on an epic) that exceed clipboard limits. The file matches what copy yields, including the `+proxy` block when that toggle is on. Filename: `<identifier>-<promptName>.md`.

### Available Prompt Templates (17 total)

**Default Prompts** (shown for every issue, including completed/canceled):
- `look-into` - look into: Quick overview and context for any task
- `research` - research: Investigate unknowns and gather information
- `plan` - plan: Step-by-step implementation with test coverage
- `implementation` - implement: Active coding phase guidance

**More Prompts** (behind "more" toggle):
- `blocked` - blocked: Analyze and resolve blockers
- `bug` - bug: Find root cause and potential fixes
- `triage` - triage: Review and update metadata (labels, priority)
- `breakdown` - breakdown: Break large tasks into actionable subtasks
- `scoping` - scoping: Define boundaries and success criteria
- `design` - design: Evaluate approaches and recommend architecture
- `spike` - spike: Time-boxed exploration for proof-of-concept
- `context` - context: Synthesize current state when joining mid-task
- `plan-review` - plan-review: Verify a plan's grounding claims with fresh context before implementation starts
- `review` - review: Verify implementation before merge
- `close-out` - close-out: Discharge the review ledger, then merge, set Done, post the summary, and file follow-ups
- `retro` - retro: Retrospective look-back (or in-flight reorient) — reconstruct what happened, assess downstream effects/risks, surface lessons; presents findings without writing back
- `retrospective-audit` - retrospective audit: Audit a merged change's claims and test integrity after the fact; presents findings without writing back

### Public Templates Page

All 17 templates above (never the meta-prompt) are also published, unauthenticated, at `/templates` — a public page with no session/workspace requirement, linked from every other page's footer (`a.footer-legal[href="/templates"]`; on `/templates` itself the footer shows it as plain current-page `<strong>` text, not a link). Each template renders in a `.prompt-card`, with its full text inside that card's `<details class="prompt-details"><pre class="prompt-text">` — so fetching the HTML is enough to read every template, no JavaScript required. The `.template-copy-btn` copy control is **not** in the served HTML: `/templates.js` injects one per card on `DOMContentLoaded` (client-only; no dispatch, no proxy token), so with JS off the cards and their text remain, minus the copy buttons. Indexable (no `noindex`) — unlike `/kpis`/`/styleguide`, discoverability is the point.

### More Prompts Inline
Access additional prompt templates from any issue, regardless of its labels or state.
A "more" link appears after visible prompts; clicking reveals all remaining prompts inline.
Prompts (including `retro`) are available on completed/canceled issues too.

**DOM Selectors:**
- `.more-toggle[data-issue-id]` - "more" link (appears after visible prompts)
- `[data-more-for="{id}"]` - hidden span containing additional prompt links

**Usage:**
1. Expand any issue with promptable labels
2. Click "more" link at end of labels row
3. Additional prompts appear inline (same comma-separated format)
4. Click any prompt to load it into the prompt container

### AI Recommendation Selectors
- `.suggest-btn` - AI suggest button (in Prompts section, requires OpenRouter)
- `.recommend-container[data-recommend-for="{id}"]` - recommendation result container
- `.recommend-reasoning` - AI reasoning text
- `.recommend-prompt` - generated prompt text
- `.free-tier-info` / `[data-testid="free-tier-info"]` - free tier usage info below recommendation
- `.free-tier-limit-reached` - error message when daily limit exceeded
- `[data-free-tier-status]` - free tier status on settings page
- `[data-free-tier-usage]` - free tier usage display on settings page

## Dispatched Sessions (Swipe)
- `GET /workspace/{urlKey}/api/sessions/{identifier}` → `{ sessions: [...] }` (newest-first dispatch loops for one issue, with feedback)
- Swipe card "Dispatched Sessions [N]" accordion (`data-accordion="sessions"`); shown only when the `dispatch` feature flag is on. `[N]` count is baked into the card server-side.

## Collective (experimental)

The Collective page (`/workspace/{urlKey}/collective`) dispatches full Claude Code sessions — one per chosen character (persona) — into one Yap chat channel for a watched cross-project discussion. Each character is bound to a connected workspace/repo. Requires the per-user `collective` feature flag; surfaced only via a link in Settings.

### Collective DOM Structure
```
main.collective-page[data-url-key]      - page container
  .collective-char-check[value]         - character selection checkbox (value = character id)
  [data-testid=collective-char-repo]    - define-new: connected-repo select
  [data-testid=collective-char-{role|lens|objective|value|disposition}] - persona inputs
  [data-testid=collective-char-add]     - add the defined character to the picker
  #collective-channel                   - Yap channel input (random default: #word-word-YYYY-MM-DD)
  #collective-topic                     - discussion topic textarea
  #collective-target                    - dispatch target select (cli | web)
  #collective-start                     - start-discussion button
  #collective-view-prompt               - build & show the participant prompt
  #collective-prompt-preview / #collective-prompt-copy - prompt preview + copy
  #collective-transcript                - live message log (ul)
  #collective-say-input / #collective-say-btn - inject human input
```

### Collective Endpoints
- `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/collective/start` — fan-out `{ workspaceUrlKeys[], channel, topic, target }`
- `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/collective/preview` — `{ channel, topic }` → `{ prompt }` (view/copy, no dispatch)
- `GET  /workspace/{urlKey}/api/collective/state?channel=&since=` — poll the channel; messages normalized to `{ id, nick, text, type, timestamp }`
- `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/collective/say` — `{ channel, message }`
- `window.__COLLECTIVE_DATA__` carries `{ urlKey, defaultChannel, yapConfigured }`

## Autopilot Observation (first-class)

The Autopilot Observation page (`/workspace/{urlKey}/observation`) is a realtime, mobile-first feed of autopilot **sessions** merged across ALL connected workspaces. First-class: a header view-switcher link (`.nav-views`, LIN-978), no feature flag (it superseded the retired experimental `dashboard` flag/view; `/workspace/{urlKey}/dashboard` now 302-redirects here). NOTE: distinct from the first-class project tree view (the "dashboard" at `/workspace/{urlKey}/`). A **session** is the LIN-591 reconstructed `sessionId` spine — an autopilot orchestrator dispatch plus every worker it spawned across the seed/epic's descended + spun-off tasks — NOT a per-task grouping. The live feed reads Mongo only (no Linear calls per poll, no LLM per poll). Session terminality follows the anchor autopilot loop (a `[done]`/`[failed]`/… feedback marker, lib/dispatch-terminal.js, folds in), so finished sessions leave the Active feed for the collapsible Completed archive.

### Autopilot Observation DOM Structure
```
main.obs-page[data-url-key]             - page container
  #obs-banner                           - status bar (holds the live poll status)
  #obs-poll-status                      - live poll status line
  #obs-chips                            - workspace filter chips (group)
    .obs-chip[data-ws].is-on            - one per workspace (data-ws = urlKey); .is-on when shown
      .obs-chip-dot[data-state]         - workspace health (worst live session status: error>running>done>queued), not on/off
  #obs-active / #obs-active-empty       - active sessions feed (ul) + empty state
  #obs-archive-toggle / #obs-archive-count  - collapsible completed archive header + count
  #obs-archive-body                     - (when open) the completed archive body
    #obs-recent / #obs-recent-empty     - completed sessions feed (ul) + empty state
      li.obs-session[data-session][data-status]  - one autopilot session
        .obs-session-head               - header container (NOT the toggle; LIN-928)
          .obs-session-topline          - header cluster: .obs-session-headmain (left) + .obs-session-side (right)
            .obs-session-headmain > .obs-session-idline  - .obs-session-dot[data-state] + .obs-session-ident (mono, ellipsizes)
            .obs-session-headmain > .obs-session-name    - bold session/seed title, truncates (omitted when it would only echo the ident)
            .obs-session-side           - fixed right column: status pill stacked above updated time
          .status-pill.status-pill--{running|done|error|queued}  - theme StatusPill (LIN-783); dot + label. done-with-warning = status-pill--done + a .status-pill__warn ⚠ marker (no 5th colour); stale → status-pill--queued
          .obs-session-summary          - one-sentence session summary (LIN-592)
          .obs-session-meta-line        - labelled runtime / model (+ workspace, task count)
          .obs-progress-row             - per-worker-run progress bar + N/M count
            .segment-bar.obs-progress > .segment-bar__cell--{running|done|error|queued}[data-live]  - theme SegmentBar cells (live cell pulses)
            .obs-progress-count         - finished/total worker-run count (N/M)
          .obs-summary-gen              - (terminal, uncached) explicit "summarise this session" button
          button.obs-disc[aria-expanded]  - disclosure control (LIN-928): click to expand/collapse ("Show run detail · N runs" / "Hide run detail")
        .obs-session-body               - (when open) objective eyebrow + status line + Level-3 drill-down
          .obs-objective                - session seed goal (design §4.6; id never reprinted)
          .obs-tasks > .obs-task        - one block per touched task (seed-first)
            .obs-task-head              - provenance tag + identifier (link when hydrated) + title + live state/labels
            .obs-rels > .obs-rel        - relationship neighborhood (parent/children/blocked by/blocks/related)
            .obs-worker-tree > li.obs-worker[data-state][data-open]  - worker-session nodes on a phase-timeline rail
              .obs-worker-node[data-state]  - phase-rail status node (✓/◐/✕/○, decorative)
              button.obs-worker-head[data-loop]  - click to expand a worker run
                .obs-worker-phase       - bordered phase tag (research/plan/implement/review…)
                .obs-worker-attempt     - "attempt N" (surfaces the run's iteration)
                .obs-worker-state[data-state]  - textual run state (complete/running/error/queued)
                .obs-worker-recap       - one-line recap (cached run-summary or agent summary)
                .obs-chips-metric > .obs-chip-metric  - bordered runtime / tool activity / artifact-count chips
              .obs-worker-body          - (when open) error box + activity log + produced-artifact links + next
                .obs-error-box          - (error runs) error-as-direction: cause + runtime + view-log link
                .obs-acts > .obs-act    - activity log rows: tool chips + right-aligned duration column
                .obs-artifacts > .obs-artifact  - icon-led produced-artifact links
                .obs-run-gen[data-loop] - (terminal, uncached) explicit "summarise this run" button
```

### Autopilot Observation Endpoints
- `GET  /workspace/{urlKey}/api/dashboard/sessions` — merged cross-workspace sessionId-grouped feed → `{ workspaces[], active[], recent[], counts, generatedAt }`; each session is workspace-tagged (`workspaceUrlKey`, `workspaceName`) and carries `{ sessionId, seedIssue, seedTitle, tasksTouched[], status, terminal, runCount, runs[], runtime, model, lastActivity }`. Each `runs[]` entry carries its Level-3 drill-down payload too — `{ loopId, issueIdentifier, issueTitle, issueUrl, agentState, stage, promptName, kind, iteration, agentSummary, runtime, metrics[], producedArtifacts[] }` (all read-only telemetry, LIN-594). Polled every 5s (visibility-gated). Mongo-only, no LLM.
- `GET  /workspace/{urlKey}/api/dashboard/loops` — merged cross-workspace flat runs → `{ workspaces[], active[], recent[], counts, generatedAt }`; each run is workspace-tagged. Polled at 5s.
- `GET|POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/dashboard/run-summary/{loopId}` — cached short run summary `{ outcome, whatHappened[], blockers[], next }`. POST forces regeneration. `GET ?cachedOnly=1` peeks the cache without generating (204 on a miss). 409 if the run is still active (terminal-only), 404 if unknown.
- `GET|POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/dashboard/session-summary/{sessionId}` — cached one-sentence session rollup (terminal-gated). A live session returns a cheap `live:true` status-line proxy (no generation). `GET ?cachedOnly=1` peeks without spending.
- `GET  /workspace/{urlKey}/api/dashboard/session-context/{sessionId}` — deterministic tasks-touched + relationship graph (lazy Linear hydration on drill-down).
- `GET  /workspace/{urlKey}/api/dashboard/hydrate/{wsUrlKey}/{identifier}` — best-effort live Linear state/labels for a session's issue (drill-down only); returns `{ hydrated: false }` rather than erroring on an expired token.
- `window.__OBSERVATION_DATA__` carries `{ urlKey, workspaces }`.

## Task Chat (experimental)

The Task Chat page (`/workspace/{urlKey}/task-chat`) lets you hold a grounded, multi-turn conversation with a single task. The task answers in the first person from its own Linear context (description, comments, subtasks, status). Requires the per-user `taskChat` feature flag; reached only via a link in Settings. Read-only (no Linear writes); history is in-browser and ephemeral.

### Task Chat DOM Structure
```
main.task-chat-page[data-url-key]      - page container
  #task-chat-id                         - task identifier input (e.g. LIN-123)
  #task-chat-transcript                 - conversation log (ul)
    li.task-chat-msg.task-chat-msg-user      - your turn
    li.task-chat-msg.task-chat-msg-assistant - the task's turn
  #task-chat-question                   - question input
  #task-chat-send                       - ask button
  #task-chat-reset                      - clear the conversation
```

### Task Chat Endpoint
- `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/task-chat/{issueId}` — SSE stream; body `{ question, history[] }`. Events: `token` (`{ token }`), `done`, `error`. Issue IDs accept identifiers like `LIN-123`.
- `window.__TASK_CHAT_DATA__` carries `{ urlKey }`.

## Flight Companion (experimental)

The Flight Companion page (`/workspace/{urlKey}/flight-companion`) is a live, in-page chat for LIN-751 ("realtime chat with work in flight"): a companion that watches the workspace's dispatch feed and checks in with you on its own client-driven cadence (visible-tab only, 30s base, doubling to a 180s cap on nothing-to-report ticks; the server's own pre-call gate is always the real spend authority), or answers directly when you send it a message. It renders through the shared chat UI (`chat.css`/`window.ChatUI`) and streams turns over SSE, including tool-use breadcrumbs (LIN-2632) via the SAME shared `window.ChatUI.toolBreadcrumbLabel` Task Chat uses — never a page-local label fork. On an auto-wake turn, a proposed follow-up renders an inline Approve/Dismiss control and only an Approve click can enqueue it — the model can never dispatch one unapproved there. On a turn you start yourself, though, the model's `send_follow_up` executes directly (no proposal card, no approval needed) — the approval gate is auto-wake-only, not a blanket guarantee. Requires the per-user `flightCompanion` feature flag; reached only via a link in Settings.

Chat is the FIRST section on the page (LIN-2443) — `How to use` and the kickoff prompt follow it, and the read-only observer report stays last. Above the thread sits a status strip (LIN-2621): model id, tools on/off (both resolved server-side ONCE per page load via `resolveWorkspaceModel`/`isToolCapableModel` — the SAME resolver the turn core uses), last check-in, next check-in due, sweep liveness/no-census, the running "this tab so far" cost total, and a mode line (`mode: read-only · proposes, never acts · rung 1 of 3`, byte-pinned; LIN-2626 turns it into a real control later). A silent auto-wake tick (one that completes with no text, the designed common outcome) paints NO chat bubble at all: instead the single, non-stacking status line (`#flight-companion-checkin`, `aria-live="polite"`, hidden until first use) reads `checking in…` for the duration of the tick, then settles to e.g. `checked in 22:03 · nothing new` on `done` — consecutive silent ticks overwrite that one node rather than appending rows, and a non-spend `gate-silent` tick refreshes the same line the same way (LIN-2632 beat 3). A turn YOU start instead gets the thinking state: an assistant row appears IMMEDIATELY, before any token or tool event, in the in-progress pill state with a quiet `thinking…` placeholder — the placeholder is display-only and never enters the client-held history, so an empty turn still ends with an honest `no reply — nothing to add` on that SAME row rather than a second one. Either way the speaker pill leaves the in-progress state on `done`/`error`.

Every `done` frame carries the turn's own summed usage (LIN-2631 sums hop usage server-side onto the FINAL `done` only). A visible turn's own bubble grows a trailing meta line (`.fc-msg-meta`, "N tokens · $x") reading exactly what that frame carried, no caveat text; the strip's running total and check-in count (LIN-2621 beat 3) accumulate on EVERY `done` this tab observes — visible or silent, any turn kind — since a silent tick's cost otherwise has nowhere to appear. `lib/openrouter.js` does not yet attach per-hop usage to a tool-using turn's intermediate frames, so a multi-hop turn's displayed cost under-reports today until that lands as its own follow-up — a known, out-of-scope gap, not a defect of this page.

Tool use is visible (LIN-2632 beat 2, "it doesn't appear to use tools?"): a `tool` event's `call` phase renders a quiet breadcrumb row (`↳ <label> …`, `.fc-inline-note`), correlated by the event's own `id` to the matching `result` (which settles it — drops the ellipsis, keeps the call-time label) or `error` (which marks it, recomputed as `<name> failed: <reason>`) that closes it out; a `proposed` event still renders the Approve/Dismiss card instead, and `cap` still shows the tool-call-limit note. A `list_pending_decisions` result ALSO renders each returned decision as an option-button card (`.fc-decision`, LIN-2621 beat 4) in the thread, reusing the rulings tab's own primitive (`window.ChatUI.appendOptions`, `chat.css`'s `.chat-options*`) verbatim — no fork. Breadcrumbs are notes, not bubbles — they never enter chat history and never trigger bubble creation on their own; on a user-initiated turn a breadcrumb arriving mid-hop inserts BEFORE the (already-present) thinking/answer row, reading `you → ↳ tool → the answer`.

**Narrow viewports (≤600px) take the phone shape** (Shape B, LIN-1412 D2 / LIN-2632 beat 4): `.flight-companion-chat-section` becomes an ordinary (non-positioned) `height: 100dvh` column — the thread grows to fill the available height (chat.css's `--chat-thread-max-height` overridden to `none` here, rather than the shared 40vh default) instead of sitting in a short box, and the composer ends up flush with the viewport's own bottom edge as the column's last child once scrolled to, staying anchored even as a software keyboard shrinks the visual viewport (the `dvh` unit, not `vh`). No `position` of its own is needed: the page's own shared header (`.nav-bar`) is already `position: sticky`, which closes the header-height gap for free. `How to use` / `Kickoff prompt` / `Latest observer report` fold below — genuinely reachable (clickable, not merely geometrically in the viewport) by scrolling past the chat section. An earlier revision made the section itself `position: sticky`, which review (LIN-2632 finding F2) found pinned it over those sections for nearly the whole page scroll instead — fixed by dropping `position` entirely. This is a per-surface override of chat.css's own documented `--chat-thread-max-height` contract, not a fork of it — chat.css itself is untouched, so every other `.chat-thread`/`.chat-composer` consumer (Task Chat, Collective, the session reply surface) is unaffected. Above 600px the page is unstyled by this rule (Shape A: the thread stays inside the ordinary scrolling page).

Since LIN-2620 the companion is also reachable directly over the workspace API proxy — `POST /api/proxy/flight-companion/turn` (`read` scope, billed to the token creator's own OpenRouter key) — so an agent can drive a turn without a browser tab at all: send `message`/`history` for a normal turn, or omit `message` for a message-less check-in tick (its own reservation instance, `stream: true` for the identical SSE frames or the default aggregated JSON body). It is always propose-only regardless of message presence — a model-proposed follow-up still waits for a human on the session-authed approve endpoint. See `GET /api/proxy/instructions` for the full request/response shape.

The page also surfaces a copyable kickoff prompt (`lib/prompts/flight-companion-kickoff.js`) that you paste into a real Claude Code session with a `readWrite` proxy token, for when a full agent session — not just chat — is wanted. Since LIN-2618 the two are no longer separate mechanisms with separate copy: both render the SAME brief (`lib/prompts/flight-companion-brief.js`) — one persona, one disposition, one readout shape, one surfacing policy, one vocabulary, one propose-then-wait gate — and differ only in transport, the kickoff adding its proxy setup and curl catalog, the chat adding its tool names, the census seed, the clock and the turn kind. What is still separate is the SESSION each drives, not what the companion is. It monitors the same dispatch feedback stream (`GET /api/proxy/dispatch?status=taken` — plus its companion `GET /api/proxy/dispatch?status=blocked` for runs parked waiting on a human, which since LIN-2079 no longer appear under `status=taken` — and `GET /api/proxy/dispatch/{id}`, NOT the browser-cookie observation endpoints). When the per-user `proxy` feature flag is also on, a `+proxy` toggle appears next to `copy prompt` (the shared `ProxyToggle` seam, LIN-1764): with it active, copy mints a single-use bootstrap token and appends the Workspace API access block automatically instead of requiring a manually-minted token. Since LIN-2443 the prompt TEXT sits inside a `<details class="disclosure">` collapsed by default; `copy prompt`, the `+proxy` toggle and the copy-status text stay OUTSIDE it and are always actionable, so copying never requires expanding the disclosure (the copy path reads the `<pre>`'s `textContent`, which a closed `<details>` still has).

### Flight Companion DOM Structure
```
main.flight-companion-page[data-url-key]  - page container
  section.flight-companion-chat-section   - "Chat" — the FIRST section (LIN-2443).
```

### Flight Companion Endpoints
- `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/flight-companion/turn` — SSE chat turn; body `{ message?, history[] }` (an absent/empty `message` is an auto-wake tick, never a client-asserted flag). Events: `token`, `tool` (`phase`: `call`/`result`/`error`/`cap`/`proposed`), `done` (an auto-wake `done` carries `surface`), `error`. A non-spend auto-wake tick returns plain JSON `{ turnKind, spent:false, reason }` instead of streaming.
- `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/flight-companion/boot` — SSE boot (orient) turn (LIN-2622), driven by `#flight-companion-start`/`#flight-companion-reorient`; body `{ history[] }` only — `message`/turn kind/`followUpMode`/budget are all endpoint-hardcoded server-side, never read from the body (the same "never client-asserted" rule as `/turn`). Propose-only (never executes a follow-up), its own budget (5 tool iterations / 2500 tokens) and lease, and it charges the free tier with the SAME 429 shape a typed turn gets — never auto-wake's silent refusal. Same SSE frame set as `/turn` (`token`/`tool`/`done`/`error`), consumed by the identical client stream reader — no boot-specific parsing exists.
- `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/flight-companion/approve-follow-up` — body `{ sessionId, prompt }`; enqueues the follow-up the model proposed on a prior auto-wake turn.

A decision-card tap (`.fc-decision`, LIN-2621 beat 4) is NOT a Flight-Companion-specific endpoint: it reuses the general `POST /workspace/{urlKey}/api/comments/{issueId}` write via `window.ReplyDelivery.postComment` — the same session-auth reply path the rulings tab and `public/scan.js`'s answer form already use. A loop-anchored decision (resumable/gone) also best-effort-stamps `markDecisionAnswered` (`decisionLoopId`/`decisionId` in the body); a task-bound decision posts a plain, unstamped comment, since the tool result carries no raw issue UUID for `taskDecisionsStore.markOutcome` to match against — a named limitation, not a defect.

## Passage Planner (experimental)

The Passage Planner page (`/workspace/{urlKey}/passage-planner`) is Flight Companion parity (LIN-1849) for the Passage Planner prompt. It surfaces the validated live passage-planning session kickoff prompt (`lib/prompts/passage-planner-kickoff.js`, which reads `docs/passage-planner-prompt.md` at HEAD with its design-artifact preamble stripped) that you paste into a fresh Claude Code session with a `readWrite` proxy token to orient off the real state of the workspace and negotiate a small ratified passage of work together. Requires the per-user `passagePlanner` feature flag; reached only via a link in Settings. Unlike Flight Companion, there is no user-facing `+proxy` toggle — the prompt requires the access block, so copy always attempts a FORCED append (`ProxyToggle.maybeAppend(text, urlKey, {force:true})`) when the per-user `proxy` feature flag is also on. When `proxy` is off, the page renders a degradation notice (with a Settings link) and copy skips the mint attempt entirely, copying the bare prompt instead of attempting a mint that would 403.

### Passage Planner DOM Structure
```
main.passage-planner-page[data-url-key]   - page container
  body[data-proxy-available]              - "true"/"false", read by the copy handler
  #passage-planner-prompt                 - the kickoff prompt (pre, copyable)
  #passage-planner-copy                   - copy-to-clipboard button
  #passage-planner-copy-feedback          - copy status text
```

## Live Console (experimental)

The Live Console page (`/workspace/{urlKey}/live-console`) is an ambient, "lean-back" realtime feed of agent activity merged across ALL connected workspaces. It has TWO sources, shaped by `lib/live-console.js`: the agent-status log (research/implementation/review/close-out steps → the event STREAM) and lean dispatch loops (running loops → currently-working LANES carrying their latest HEARTBEAT — tool count / elapsed / per-tool breakdown — plus `[evidence]` artifacts as linked stream events; heartbeat beats also feed the tempo sparkline so it keeps moving between discrete steps). Reads Mongo only — no Linear calls and no LLM per poll. Requires the per-user `liveConsole` feature flag; reached via a Settings link and the nav `⋯ more` overflow when on (route redirects to `/settings` when off). Polls every 5s (chained, in-flight-guarded, exponential backoff on failure; pauses while the tab is hidden). A "view earlier activity" control pages OLDER status events (before page load) into a history region below the live feed. Purely presentational — no writes.

### Live Console DOM Structure
```
main.lc-page[data-url-key]                    - page container
  [data-testid="live-console-banner"]         - status banner
    #live-console-dot[data-health]            - health dot (live|done|error|idle)
    #live-console-status[aria-live=polite]    - one-line fleet status / connection state
  .lc-pulse-section                           - flowing activity strip section (LIN-1505 Phase C: zoom controls)
    [data-testid="live-console-pulse-presets"][role=group][aria-label="Strip range"]  - 3m/15m/1h/6h
                                                range buttons (reuses .lc-timeline-preset styling verbatim);
                                                3m is the always-on-load default, never data-dependent
      [data-testid="live-console-pulse-preset-3m|15m|1h|6h"][data-range][aria-pressed]  - one per rung
    #live-console-pulse-span-text               - visible "last N minutes/hours" label, kept in sync
                                                with the active span (same phrasing convention as the
                                                timeline's window label)
    .lc-pulse > #live-console-tempo             - full-width flowing activity strip <canvas>: scrolls
                                                right→left in real time (now = right edge, NEVER pans —
                                                zoom only); a soft heartbeat "hum" area under colour-coded
                                                event blips that drift left and fade. rAF-animated,
                                                reduced-motion aware (static snapshot instead of
                                                scrolling, but a preset/gesture still repaints immediately).
                                                Zoom: ctrl/meta+wheel (desktop) or two-finger pinch
                                                (touch) on `.lc-pulse` itself, gated identically to the
                                                timeline's; deliberately NO one-finger gesture here — a
                                                one-finger vertical swipe over the strip still scrolls the
                                                page (`touch-action: pan-y`, unlike the timeline's `none`).
                                                Independent of the timeline's own zoom/pan — never coupled,
                                                never shares state or constants with it.
  [data-testid="live-console-chips"]          - workspace filter chips (hidden when <2 workspaces)
    .lc-chip[data-ws][aria-pressed]           - one toggle per workspace (.lc-chip--off when filtered out)
  .lc-timeline-section                        - swimlane timeline: recent dispatch runs as bars, default
                                                window is an auto-fit view latched at first paint (clamped to
                                                a 1h floor), zoomable/pannable (LIN-1743); the axis' fixed
                                                bound stays the server's 24h data window (LIN-1742/LIN-1928)
    .lc-timeline-presets                      - fit/1h/24h range buttons; the section label, its aria-label,
                                                and the empty-state text below all reflect whichever window is
                                                actually active, not a literal "24 hours" (LIN-1928)
    #live-console-timeline-axis               - time axis mount, same page column as the label above (no full-bleed breakout)
    [data-testid="live-console-timeline"]     - bars viewport (internal vertical scroll, no row cap)
      [data-testid="live-console-timeline-connectors"]  - SVG overlay: one curved path per
                                                run-to-run connector (server `timeline.connectors`
                                                {fromId,toId} edges), sits behind the bars, skipped
                                                when either endpoint bar is hidden
      [data-testid="live-console-timeline-bar"][data-kind][data-ws]  - one bar per run;
                                                data-kind vocabulary matches the stream's (below);
                                                .lc-timeline-bar--clipped marks a run whose true start
                                                predates the 24h window (clipped to the left edge, not dropped);
                                                .lc-timeline-bar-label child renders the visible
                                                "ticket identifier — kind/promptName" text (title/
                                                aria-label carry the same string)
  [data-testid="live-console-lanes"]          - "working now" rail (<ul>)
    [data-testid="live-console-lane"]         - one breathing lane per working agent
      a.lc-lane-task[href]                     - links to that workspace's /observation
      [data-testid="live-console-heartbeat"]  - live tool-count/elapsed/breakdown tick (empty when none);
                                                escaped HTML — an idle beat (state:'idle') shows an
                                                Observation-style ".obs-act-chip.obs-act-idle" "no tools"
                                                chip instead of the numeric count
  [data-testid="live-console-stream"]         - live activity stream (<ol>, newest first)
    [data-testid="live-console-event"][data-kind]  - one event; data-kind: done|working|blocked|failed|evidence|info
      a.lc-event-task[href]                    - links to that workspace's /observation
      a.lc-event-summary-link[href]            - (evidence only) links to the produced artifact
  [data-testid="live-console-history"]        - paged-in OLDER events (<ol>, below the live stream)
  [data-testid="live-console-more"]           - "view earlier activity" pager button
```
- `data-kind` vocabulary: `done` (✓), `working` (◐), `blocked` (◑), `failed` (✗), `evidence` (↗), `info` (·) — colour AND glyph carry the state (never colour alone).
- New events on later polls get a transient `.lc-event--new` class; lane pulses + heartbeat ticks persist across polls via a keyed reconcile (nodes are updated in place, not rebuilt).

### Live Console Endpoint
- `GET /workspace/{urlKey}/api/live-console/events` — merged, normalized live feed (session-auth; 403 when the flag is off). Returns `{ events:[{id,kind,ts,iso,workspaceUrlKey,workspaceName,task,action,status,summary,url}], lanes:[{workspaceUrlKey,workspaceName,task,action,summary,sinceMs,lastActivityMs,heartbeat:{toolCount,elapsedSeconds,breakdown,total,state}}], tempo:[n,...], pulse:{bucketMs,endTs,buckets:[n,...],load:[n,...]}, timeline:{rows:[[{id,issueIdentifier,kind,promptName,outcomeKind,start,end,stillRunning,clippedStart,groupKey,followUpTo,workspaceUrlKey,connectorTruncated},...],...], connectors:[{fromId,toId},...], truncated, totalInWindow}, serverNow, summary:{active,done,failed,blocked,total}, hasMore, oldestTs }`. `pulse` is heartbeat-only fine-grained density (the strip's hum); `serverNow` anchors the strip's time axis (also the timeline's view-window right edge, whichever window is active). `timeline.rows` is pre-packed into non-overlapping display rows (`lib/live-console.js`'s `packTimelineRows`, LIN-1908 Phase A: a two-level pack — same-session runs pack within their own group-row as before, then group-rows from EVERY session are first-fit across groups, sorted by start ascending, admitting a group-row into a shared display row only when it starts at least `TIMELINE_ROW_BUFFER_MS` (~8.6min) past that row's current end) — each row is an array of runs never overlapping in time, but a row no longer means "one session lineage" (it can hold several unrelated short sessions) and rows are emitted in ascending-start creation order, not most-recently-active-first; `outcomeKind` (not dispatch `kind`) is the colour source; `end:null` + `stillRunning:true` is an open-ended (still-running) bar; `stillRunning:'unknown'` is a stale-but-not-yet-terminal run; `truncated`/`totalInWindow` disclose when the 500-run cap dropped older rows (LIN-1494 pattern). Generation-free. LIN-1908 Phase C: `pulse.load[]` is additive alongside `buckets[]` — same length/anchors, each bucket summing its beats' `toolCount` (falling back to `total`) rather than counting `+= 1` — so the client can render magnitude nested inside the beat-count hum area on its own decaying scale, never replacing `buckets[]`'s own meaning; `heartbeat.state` (`'running'|'idle'|null`, from `lib/session-telemetry.js`'s `parseHeartbeat`) is likewise additive and surfaces as an escaped idle chip on a lane's heartbeat tick when `'idle'`.
- `GET …/events?before=<epochMs>&limit=<n>` — a HISTORY page: older status events strictly before the cursor. Returns `{ events:[…], hasMore, oldestTs }`.

## Common Workflows

1. **Find in-progress tasks**: Look in "In Progress" section at top (displays as tree with subtasks)
2. **Drill into project**: Click project header to expand, click task to see details
3. **Expand subtasks**: Click parent task or ▶ arrow to show child tasks (works in both sections)
4. **Filter by team**: Use team selector in nav bar
5. **Search for issues**: Click "search" in nav bar (or press "/"), type keywords to filter issues across all sections
6. **Open in provider**: Expand task, click the "View in {provider} →" link (text is dynamic, e.g. "View in Linear")
7. **View task details**: Expand task, click "Details ▶" to show description and metadata
8. **Generate prompt for task**: Expand task, click "Prompts ▶" to reveal prompt buttons, click a prompt button, copy the generated prompt
9. **Get AI recommendation**: Expand task, click "Prompts ▶", click "AI suggest" button (free tier: 20/day per workspace)

## Limitations

- Read-only view (no editing tasks)
- Logout requires re-authentication via Linear OAuth
- Expand/collapse state persists in localStorage (reset restores defaults)
- Team filter selection persists in localStorage across sessions
- Landing page (`/`, unauthenticated) is a bespoke Harbour showcase — a brand hero, fake-data glimpses of real surfaces (observation feed, swim board, grounded prompt), a "try it yourself" low-cost trial callout, a providers strip, and a distinct Harbour OS section. It is NOT the project-tree renderer; section blocks carry `[data-testid="landing-{loop,observation,swim,prompt,try,providers,os}"]`. The `/swipe` and `/swim` unauthenticated previews still render sample tree data.
